name: Klipgat

queries.query: Klipgat South Africa official cadastral map parcel GIS land registry North West municipality Chief Surveyor General
queries.scope: Find official local cadastral registry/map evidence and test anonymous parcel geometry access.
queries.result: Anonymous point query against the official CSG-hosted Erven polygon layer returns one active parcel covering the WUP point. A safe exact-ID query returned a valid five-vertex polygon (about 299.9 m² in EPSG:32735). Esri JSON works; the same service’s GeoJSON query returns HTTP 200 with ArcGIS error 400, so the existing GeoJSON-only adapter is incompatible and no production qualification is claimed.
queries.executionMethod: Separate English and local-language web searches followed by official portal and bounded public service review.

source.name: Chief Surveyor-General National Cadastral Layer — Erven
source.operator: Chief Surveyor-General; Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment hosts the ArcGIS service
source.serviceType: Anonymous ArcGIS REST polygon layer; safe Esri JSON feature queries succeed. GeoJSON output fails with `Failed to execute query`.
source.layer: Chief Surveyor-General National Cadastral Layer — Erven
source.nativeIdEvidence: One official registered Erven feature covers the exact WUP point. This single exact-point result establishes local sample coverage only, not citywide completeness.
source.scope: 201 valid, distinct Chief Surveyor-General Erven references verified in thirteen bounded cells around the unchanged ranked Klipgat WUP locator. The official DFFE-hosted service advertises GeoJSON but rejects that format in actual queries; explicit native Esri JSON queries succeed. A strict reader preserves every straight-ring coordinate and assigns native holes/components without repair; native curve representations and unsupported or ambiguous rings remain unavailable. Complete object-ID manifests, forced three-row paging (42 rows over fourteen pages), all 201 fresh native PRCL_KEY reads, explicit absence, footprint and source binding passed. Independent GEOS audit in EPSG:32735 found no invalid geometries, duplicates, sampled overlaps above 0.01 m² or operation errors. The sampled records all have publisher statuses R/C/E; no guessed lifecycle filter is applied. Citywide completeness, legal title, survey accuracy and broader identity uniqueness remain unverified.
